newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Hart says trialists selected on form.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Hart says trialists selected on form.

text.p: AUCKLAND, May 20 - The form of players in the Super 12 and last year's 10 tests were the main criteria for All Black trial team selections, coach John Hart said on Tuesday.
The two teams, the shadow test side as New Zealand Barbarians and the second 15 as New Zealand A were named today for the match in Rotorua on June 8.
Hart said a number of players were unlucky to have missed out but he was pleased that it meant there was some genuine depth in areas of concern.

The shadow test side have only six reserves, in line with international rules, while the New Zealand A team have eight reserves. Hart said he preferred a 23-member squad for home tests and this has been approved by New Zealand rugby.
"It was the Super 12 form and the 1996 test series form that we chose players from. In some cases 1996 test players have shown that they're right up there," Hart told NZPA.
He said the match would not be played as a trial, rather a match, because he thought the days of the Probables and the Possibles teams were gone.

Hart said the shadow All Blacks, with two changes from last year's regular test side, were being given every opportunity to regain their combination while NZ A would have the opportunity to press for a place in the 36-member squad to tour Britain at the end of the year.
"If you have a look at the NZ A team reserves there are a number of youngsters who we think are very promising."
Hart said four players from last year's All Black squad not named in the 44 today were told this morning the reasons why they had not been chosen.
The players were Wellington Hurricanes prop Phil Coffin, Waikato Chiefs fullback Matthew Cooper, Canterbury Crusaders centre Tabai Matson and Otago highlanders first five-eighth Simon Culhane.
He said Auckland's Lee Stensness showed in last year's New Zealand Barbarians match against England and in this year's Super 12 that he would fit his test team.
"He has all the skills and the ability and flexibility to play the game at this level."

Charles Riechelmann, although not having much experience at blindside flanker, gained the nod in the shadow test side because the selectors felt he had much to offer in the position. He also provided ideal cover at lock.
Young Auckland prop Paul Thomson was a contender for the tour of South Africa last year, but after a series of games around the country the selectors felt he hadn't matured enough.
"But he has shown this year that he has come on in leaps and bounds," Hart said after including Thomson in the New Zealand A team.
Hart said the selectors could change the lineups depending on the Blues' and the Hurricanes Super 12 playoff games over the next two weeks.
